definitions.explanation: A category of Japanese sweets made by steaming dough or batter, often containing bean paste or other fillings.

examples.japanese: {蒸|む}し{菓子|がし}を{作|つく}る。
{秋|あき}は{蒸|む}し{菓子|がし}がおいしい{季節|きせつ}だ。
examples.english: Autumn is the season when steamed sweets are delicious.

examples.japanese: {和菓子屋|わがしや}で{栗|くり}{蒸|む}し{羊羹|ようかん}などの{蒸|む}し{菓子|がし}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought steamed sweets like chestnut steamed yōkan at the Japanese confectionery shop.

notes:
Compound of {蒸|む}す (to steam) and {菓子|かし} (confection), where かし becomes がし by rendaku. One of the main categories of {和菓子|わがし} (Japanese sweets), alongside {焼|や}き{菓子|がし} (baked sweets) and {生菓子|なまがし} (fresh sweets).

EXAMPLES OF {蒸|む}し{菓子|がし}:
- {饅頭|まんじゅう}: steamed bun with sweet filling
- {蒸|む}し{羊羹|ようかん}: steamed yōkan (jelly)
- {薯蕷饅頭|じょうよまんじゅう}: steamed bun made with yam dough
- ういろう: uirō (steamed rice-flour cake)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {焼|や}き{菓子|がし}: baked confection — sweets made by baking rather than steaming
- {干菓子|ひがし}: dry confection — pressed or dried sweets with very low moisture
- {生菓子|なまがし}: fresh confection — moist sweets with high water content, eaten fresh
